34-year-old male presents to the outpatient clinic complaining of progressive pain in his right foot for the last 3 months. The pain initially occurred only on walking for long distances but now occurs after walking about 50 meters and is relieved by rest. For the last 2 weeks, he has also noticed pain in his toes even at rest, especially at night. He is a heavy smoker (20 cigarettes/day for 15 years). He has no history of diabetes mellitus or hypertension. On examination: The right foot pale with small painful ulcer on the tip of the big toe. Dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses on the right side are weak and difficult to palpate. Sensation is intact and motor power is normal. (9 Marks) A. What is the most likely diagnosis? B.
